- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.27 or +0.32) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.11 or -0.16 over multiple days) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustments after a spike, especially if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment weakens.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2025 (e.g., 2025-09-15–18) — model fails to account for short-term volatility and sentiment decay.
- Overshoot after positive sentiment peaks — model assumes momentum continues, but sentiment often reverses or cools quickly.
